topic: Decarbonizing the Skies – Technology Development for Sustainable Aviation Fuel
title: Decarbonizing the Skies – Technology Development for Sustainable Aviation Fuel
abstract: Decarbonizing the aviation sector remains a critical need that requires low-carbon intensity, fungible, liquid hydrocarbon fuels, commonly referred to as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). This talk will address technology development and scale-up efforts at Alder Fuels for producing SAF, with a focus on biogenic waste conversion pathways that produce drop-in hydrocarbon biofuel. Motivation for expanding SAF feedstocks beyond fats, oil, and grease will be addressed, as well as Alder’s strategy to generate low carbon biocrude oil that is compatible with downstream hydroprocessing within the existing refinery infrastructure. Technical findings will be presented on Alder’s process engineering and scale-up work conducted jointly with the Department of Energy and industry partners. Jet fuel property considerations will be discussed for guiding SAF process development, as well as approaches to meet ASTM specifications while increasing the renewable blend content of jet fuel towards 100% SAF.

authors: Derek Vardon | Alder Fuels, LLC, Washington, DC

topic: Anything to SAF - Innovations and the Challenges Ahead
title: Anything to SAF - Innovations and the Challenges Ahead
abstract: Renewable fuel mandates and incentives around the world have created demand for sustainable 2nd generation biofuels and opportunities for fuel producers and project developers to make drop-in compatible biofuels. Demand is growing and is expected to accelerate in the coming years. Thus far Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) demand has only begun to penetrate markets, as very small quantities are produced in the US and worldwide. However, achieving government targets for adoption by 2030 will require SAF demand to grow to 3 billion gallons/year (GPY) in North America and 1.5 billion GPY in Europe. Demand is expected to continue growing after 2030, as government targets and mandates are expected to drive further adoption. Honeywell UOP is a leader in providing technology to produce renewable fuels. Our Ecofining TM technology, commercialized in 2013, has enabled the significant capacity of renewable diesel that meet summer and winter specifications, and SAF product that meets ASTMD7566 specifications for Synthetic Paraffinic Kerosene (SPK) from Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids (HEFA). More recently, we have also developed technologies to convert alternate renewable feedstocks like ethanol or cellulosic biomass to produce SAF and Renewable Diesel. This talk will discuss the various technologies in our portfolio for making SAF and highlight the challenges that still lie ahead.
presenting_author: Eseoghene Jeroro | Honeywell/UOP, Des Plaines, IL
authors: Eseoghene Jeroro | Honeywell/UOP, Des Plaines, IL

topic: Renewable Methanol Conversion to Lower Emission Fuels and Sustainable Chemicals
title: Renewable Methanol Conversion to Lower Emission Fuels and Sustainable Chemicals
abstract: Renewable MeOH, as a versatile and lower carbon intensity (CI) intermediate, is anticipated to be produced in greater volumes during the energy transition. Advanced methanol conversion technology is a key enabler to address the world’s growing demand for a range of lower emission fuels and lower CI chemicals. ExxonMobil’s recent methanol conversion technology efforts have been focused on developing and deploying fully integrated scalable solutions to sustainable products from renewable methanol as the feedstock. This presentation will highlight key renewable methanol conversion technology learnings on 1) advantaged catalyst choices in producing flexible product slates, and 2) optimal reactor designs and process development for improving product yield and selectivity. Finally, opportunities such as tailoring yield of specific molecules and further reducing capital cost and CI in methanol-to-sustainable products will be elaborated on to provide insights on future R&D directions in commercialization of renewable MeOH conversion technologies.

topic: Scaling up Single-Step Carbon Dioxide Conversion Technology for Sustainable Products
title: Scaling up Single-Step Carbon Dioxide Conversion Technology for Sustainable Products
abstract: Air Company has scaled up a single-step process for hydrogenation of carbon dioxide using green hydrogen from a benchtop proof-of-concept to a pilot system, that consumes as much as 1 ton per day of carbon dioxide and produces ethanol that is used in hand sanitizer, fragrance, spirits, and other products. In this talk, additional detail will be given to discussion on progressing from the lab-scale to small commercial scales at Air Company over the last 4-5 years, with focus on the challenges and opportunities experienced along the way. Central to the process is the novel and proprietary catalyst that drives the chemistry and the reactor design that enables scale. The process for deployment of our pilot plant, its 24/7 operation, and our journey forward scaling our technology toward world-scale will also be included.

title: SAF- Prometheus Fuels
abstract: Tech transfer from academic institutions to commercial deployment has been described crossing the “valley of death” because of the poor functioning and low success rates of this transfer. This talk will discuss the causes of the disfunction in this pathway, as well as the changes that can substantially increase success in tech transfer. The talk will be based on the authors experience in transitioning from a PhD in Engineering on an academic career path to being a successful entrepreneur who has founded a unicorn startup based on materials science, nanotechnology, and separations technologies.
